Good catch, fixed. Removed the environment-specific defaults: `BucketName` no longer has a default and now requires explicit input, and the `SentinelSQSQueueName` default (the `RnD` one) is gone too. This also makes the template consistent with the CloudTrail and GuardDuty templates, where the bucket and queue names already require input.

Worth noting the bucket default in particular was a latent failure: S3 bucket names are globally unique, so anyone deploying with the old default would have collided with an already-claimed name. Requiring input is the right fix here rather than a placeholder default, since a placeholder would just shift the collision to whoever deploys first.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed by removing the unused `FlowLogsPrefix` parameter and the `UseCustomPrefix` condition. I went with removal rather than wiring up prefix filtering: a hardcoded prefix filter in the S3 notification would silently drop notifications if a deployment's flow logs use a different layout (Hive-compatible prefixes, a custom delivery prefix, etc.), and Sentinel would receive nothing with no obvious error. The `.gz` suffix filter already in place is the safer, more permissive boundary.
